desert_p06_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_001.text: The shortest line to the house crossed a hollow crusted white as bone. Tuo led the caravan around it on the dark ridge road, where wheels had cut shallow channels in exposed stone. The building appeared and disappeared between spurs. Every glimpse made it seem close; every turn demanded another piece of walking. Han stopped predicting arrival after his second mistake. Yue appreciated that more than a third encouraging estimate. She could see the broken roof through her lowered screens, a shape that now occupied hours rather than the easy finger-width it had taken on paper.

desert_p06_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_002.text: At the midday halt Bao checked the crew before they began the final descent. Heat had sharpened the light reflected from the hollow. The water portions increased again, and the drivers sheltered the mules beneath the overlapping cart panels. The camp worker's wrist was improving; he could manage light lines but not hammering. Yue shared a piece of preserved fish with the quiet driver and asked why she chose the equipment cart. The woman said tools complained less than passengers, provided they were packed well. Yue glanced at the sighting case.

desert_p06_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_003.text: The driver added that a silent complaint could still become an expensive one. Gao sat on a black rock with the field book closed across her knees. Du stood nearby, trying to identify the north-facing window against an old sketch. The roofline differed. A high central ridge had vanished, and the remaining western section leaned toward the courtyard. Tuo remembered the ridge intact, but could not place the year. Han asked whether this was definitely their commissioned building. Gao said the location and stairs fitted Crescent House; the customer's courtyard sketch might describe another structure in the same station group.

desert_p06_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_004.text: The report would need to resolve that before attaching measurements to a borrowed name.

desert_p06_005.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p06_005.text: We shall identify what stands here by its visible features first. Name comes after location, not in place of it. Tuo knows the approach. Du has the older descriptions. Yue will draw the present roofline from this ridge. I shall measure its position against the dark spur. If the customer's sketch belongs to a neighbouring structure, we can say that. I would rather return with two accurately separated places than one beautifully measured confusion. Han, your subscribers asked us to settle conflicting directions. They should not be astonished when the conflict extends as far as the destination.

desert_p06_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_006.text: Han accepted the point with an expression suggesting astonishment had already taken place privately. He gave Yue the customer's sketch to copy beside her own. Its eastern gate had three narrow openings; Crescent House showed a single broad arch, partly broken. The north stair appeared in both. Du explained that the former engineers reused their plans across several stations. An account that remembered only a stair could easily become attached to the wrong roof. Tuo pointed to a shallow notch beyond the house. A second site lay that way, mostly hidden below the ridge.

desert_p06_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_007.text: She had never taken loaded carts there. The last descent followed a curve narrow enough that the carts went down with broad gaps. Drivers held their teams straight while the farrier walked beside the leading pair. Yue waited at each turn until the equipment driver could see the red flag, then moved to the next sightline. The work kept her occupied without requiring heavy grips. Above her, the house's northern window flashed again. This time she saw a pale speck move beside it, too small to identify. A bird or loose scrap could explain the change.

desert_p06_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_008.text: She wrote neither until she had a better view. They reached the outer forecourt in late afternoon. Dark paving stones emerged from the blown grit, marked by cart wheels and the rings where tether posts once stood. Tuo chose the firmest edge for the three carts, clear of the loose roof. Gao walked the courtyard boundary with the quiet driver before shelters came off. The house's central roof had fallen inward, leaving sound exterior walls in some places and uncertain masonry in others. Its doorway admitted a long view of open sky.

desert_p06_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_009.text: The crew would camp outside rather than make an inn from the first shade that looked inviting. Before the tents were opened, the farrier found one paving slab rocking beneath an empty trough. He lifted the trough, pressed the slab's edge with his boot, and heard a hollow knock. Gao marked that patch for the carts to avoid. It lay outside the chosen gravel strip but inside the wider forecourt people might naturally wander across. Yue fetched two spare path stakes; the drivers set a line between them.

desert_p06_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_010.text: Beneath the lifted edge she could see darkness and a fragment of brick arch. The house had more below its floor than the exterior shape suggested. Du crouched beyond the marked edge, pleased by the brick fragment and irritated that pleasure should require restraint. He recognised an old drain-cover pattern from a station manual, but the opening was too narrow to identify a whole channel. Gao asked him to leave the label tentative. He did, crossing out his first confident noun. Yue drew the rocking slab from firm gravel.

desert_p06_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_011.text: A little stream of ants crossed its lower seam, carrying pale fragments toward the wall. Their route showed a gap; it did not show where a human should put a foot. She kept her pencil on the visible bricks.

desert_p06_012.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p06_012.text: The paving may cover drains or a service passage. We can report the void without deciding its entire purpose. The old stations needed access below their floors, and a missing roof changes how those spaces weather. Han, tell the drivers the gravel strip remains our cart place; nobody moves a tank onto the handsome paving to improve the view. Yue, make the boundary legible from the treatment corner too. At dusk people choose shortcuts with their eyes half occupied. We have already chosen a good camp. Let us keep choosing it after we grow tired.

desert_p06_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_013.text: The quiet driver moved a loose crate that might tempt somebody to step over the line. Han helped her, then asked the farrier whether the mules' tether sweep reached it. It did not. The farrier shortened one slack lead anyway because Plum liked testing the distance between permission and possibility. Yue held the light stake while its cord tightened. The camp worker showed her a knot she could release without dragging rough rope through her healed palms. She tried it twice, leaving enough slack to avoid pulling the stake loose.

desert_p06_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_014.text: The instruction made her useful without converting recovery into a performance. Inside the east arch, shallow grooves crossed the paving toward a small wall outlet. Gao traced them from outside the hollow patch, using the staff tip to point rather than walking along every line. The grooves were open gutters, not concealed traps. Old stations had channelled roof water away from the main entrance. Their outlets now disappeared beneath blown grit. A thin strip of grass grew beside one, greener than the basin's dry tufts. Yue noted it while the surveyor marked drainage on the exterior sketch.

desert_p06_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_015.text: The grass sample from the village suddenly belonged to more than an isolated detour. Tuo said grass grew there even in dry summers. She had seen travellers dig for water beside it and find only a bitter damp layer. The station's foundations might intercept a buried seep. Gao would compare that with the lower site's channels before offering a cause. Han asked whether the seep threatened the cart strip. Its gravel sat higher and showed no dampness. They checked beneath the tank frames after unloading, finding the joints dry.

desert_p06_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_016.text: Yue felt the difference between fear looking for any shadow and attention asking a specific question. The latter gave her something she could finish. The cook set the first kettle on his stove and watched its steam draw sideways toward the arch. He moved the stove a little farther from the old outlet, so smoke would not enter a passage full of unknown debris. The shift put it nearer the eating shade but clear of loose cloth. Bao approved after walking the route between stove and treatment corner.

desert_p06_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_017.text: Yue carried empty bowls through that route to check where people would meet. The small rehearsal was less amusing than Plum's paper theft in the yard, yet it prevented a hot kettle from becoming somebody's evening story. An old bell bracket projected above the doorway. No bell remained, though the wall beneath it held a worn patch at shoulder height where generations had pulled a rope. Yue touched nothing. She stood where a waiting traveller might have stood and looked through the arch at the road. The dark ridge cut one direction from view; the forecourt opened toward another.

desert_p06_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_018.text: Whoever designed the house had chosen a place where people could shelter without losing sight of approaching carts. The purpose remained visible after the furnishings vanished. Du came beside her and said the bell had probably governed weighing turns. Gao corrected him gently: that function belonged more likely to the lower exchange. At a wind station the bell could have announced weather observations or shift changes. Du accepted the alternatives and wrote bell bracket, use unknown. The plain phrase disappointed Yue for a moment because she had imagined the ringing so clearly.

desert_p06_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_019.text: Then she saw him leave a little blank space beside it. A missing answer did not erase the feature. It made room for whoever later found a surviving account. Their report would carry the bracket forward without forcing it into the wrong building's daily life. Han brought out the subscriber sketch again and matched its three openings to the house's single broad arch. The mismatch now looked obvious enough that he wondered how he had missed it in town. Gao said paper places were easier to merge before their walls stood in front of you.

desert_p06_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_020.text: He asked for her exact wording in the revised commission note. She wrote that the supplied sketch probably depicted the lower North Exchange, subject to location confirmation. He read it aloud, liked its caution more than expected, and left the remainder of the report page open for morning work. The cook stood beneath the eastern arch long enough to admire the cool air flowing from a narrow floor opening. Then he moved his stove to the selected outside corner. He did not need persuasion this time; the broken shelter had taught him what a convenient wall could conceal.

desert_p06_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_021.text: Yue helped spread the light shade cloth while the camp worker tied it with his good hand. The drivers used their spare tent lines to fix the corners. Nobody attached a line to the ruin. The new camp had room for the mules to turn without stepping over the sleeping places. Crescent House began making sounds as the afternoon wind crossed its broken roof. A low note rose from the northern stair, followed by a higher vibration near the courtyard opening. The driver with the wooden bird stared at his pocket as though the toy had learned to play itself.

desert_p06_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_022.text: Tuo said the house had always been noisy in this wind. Du admitted he had once described its singing in a travel essay, with more grandeur than measurement. Gao asked whether he had attributed it to ancestors. He said only metaphorical ones, which had become an expensive distinction when a reader attempted to summon them.

desert_p06_023.speaker: du_she
desert_p06_023.text: I wrote that the station remembered every caravan. The editor liked the line. A man from the southern coast came here and shouted his grandfather's name into the stair for an afternoon. He later wrote to complain that my directions were misleading. I had to agree about the shouting. I had never intended the building to keep a list of the dead. It kept pressure differences and openings arranged by practical people. The metaphor was mine. So was the responsibility for admitting that practical people had done more interesting work than I had allowed them in the essay.

desert_p06_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_024.text: Yue laughed, then looked at Tuo to see whether the joke had touched her grief. The guide's mouth was curved, though her eyes stayed on the stair. A sound could carry a person's past without anyone deliberately calling it back. The house did not require an ancestor to produce its note, and Tuo did not require an ancestor to feel it. Yue kept both thoughts while opening the field book. The first exterior sketch had no place for them.

desert_p06_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_025.text: She drew the broad east arch and the north window, placing the broken roofline against the dark ridge so its position could be recognised. Gao set the tripod on a sound paving slab outside the wall's fall zone. She took readings to the courtyard corners visible from there, then moved to a second position before accepting their relation. Yue held the rod while Du recorded the observations. Wind shook the staff occasionally; they waited through the gusts. The work differed from the yard chiefly because the building made it easy to imagine more than they had seen.

desert_p06_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_026.text: A missing corner tempted Yue to continue a line in pencil. Gao had her stop it at the last visible stone and label the continuation as uncertain. Under the broad east arch an inscription named the station's former function: wind and road measure, northern district. Several characters had been recut over an older name. Du copied both sets with patient care, using the raking light to see their edges. He asked Gao to check that his paper did not confuse a crack with a stroke.

desert_p06_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_027.text: Tuo looked at the newer district name and said people had called the place Crescent House before the recutting. The later North Exchange name belonged below the split cairn, where cargo was once weighed. The customer's sketch now had a likely home of its own.

desert_p06_028.speaker: han_xun
desert_p06_028.text: So the letters from my subscribers have joined a wind station to a weigh house and expected one building to answer. I shall enjoy explaining that after they finish complaining about our delay. Do we need the lower building to report the approach they intend to reopen? Tell me honestly. If the road reaches only this courtyard, we can say so. If their proposed loading ground lies beyond it, we need at least a safe look at the ground. I will not turn the evening into an argument about which ancient district office deserved the better name.

desert_p06_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_029.text: Gao said the intended loading ground matched the lower site. Its approach mattered to the carrier commission, but nobody needed to enter its interior merely to establish where carts could stand. Tuo could guide them to a safe overlook in the morning. Han accepted that order. Du asked to examine the wind station's visible inscriptions before sunset while the light remained useful. Gao agreed and went with him. Yue felt the report separating into pieces that could be completed rather than swelling into an obligation to know everything the old district had ever done.

desert_p06_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_030.text: Beside the north stair, Yue found the source of the window's flash: a sliver of pale glass caught in a bird's nest on the inner sill. A small brown bird stood beside it with a grass strand in its beak. Wind moved the nest's loose edge, shifting the glass toward sunlight. She showed Gao from the courtyard, without climbing to the window. The surveyor made a little note about the obstruction and left the nest untouched. The revelation pleased Yue more than an elaborate mystery would have done.

desert_p06_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_031.text: The house had acquired a tenant with no interest in the route's reputation. The staircase descended only six visible steps before turning under a fallen beam. Cool air emerged through a side grille, carrying the smell of dry stone. Gao found no reason to remove the beam. It pressed against damaged masonry, and opening the passage could unsettle more than its own weight. Du copied a small diagram engraved beside the grille: an upper shaft, a shaded chamber, a lower outlet. It matched the broken quarry shelter's surviving duct.

desert_p06_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_032.text: The sound changed when Yue stood in front of the grille; she stepped aside, realising that even looking could alter the thing she hoped to observe.

desert_p06_033.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p06_033.text: A useful mistake. You changed the airflow and heard the result. We can record that from outside. It suggests the lower outlet still connects with something open, though it does not tell us how much passage survives. We will not crawl after the answer. The weigh house may show the same arrangement where less roof has fallen. For now the exterior survey is enough. Du, take your tracing while I hold the shade. Yue, write wind from west, grille partly obstructed by fallen roof material. Leave the word haunted for whoever intends to sell another essay.

desert_p06_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_034.text: Du said the newer editors preferred mysterious to haunted. Gao replied that both cost extra when a grandfather was summoned. Yue wrote the plain description and smiled into the page. The instruction had a practical consequence: the measured airflow could explain the old station's design, perhaps the way lower chambers stayed dry. She could ask that later without inventing occupants behind every note. Bao called from camp that supper would be ready when the surveyors remembered their bodies. Du suggested she ring a bell.

desert_p06_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_035.text: The cook rang his ladle against a bowl, producing a tone uglier than anything the house had managed. The day's supply stood at one thousand two hundred and forty-five litres after one hundred and eighty-eight withdrawn. Han kept the morning eighty-litre purchase visible on the previous line. No one mistook the total for a fresh tank. The heat had demanded larger portions, and the mule watering had remained steady. Gao expected the next morning's work to be cooler in the shade of the lower ridge. She still planned a prompt return once the required observations were complete.

desert_p06_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_036.text: Yue washed her face with her allotted small portion, catching the runoff in the waste bowl so grit would not gather beside the sleeping tents. At supper the quiet driver asked the cook how he had learned to keep food pleasant after so many days of dust. He said his mother ran a river ferry kitchen, where wet passengers complained as vigorously as dry ones. The difference was mostly whether their sleeves dripped into the bowls. He had come west after the ferry moved upstream and trade no longer passed her door. She now sold breakfasts near the new landing.

desert_p06_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_037.text: He sent her money when work allowed, and she sent him criticism of recipes he had never claimed to use. Yue thought the river had followed him farther than either intended. The cook had bought the eggs because his mother's letters insisted travellers should remember meals rather than merely survive them. Han teased him for obeying criticism he claimed to resent. He answered that a man could resent sound advice and follow it all the same. Bao raised her cup in agreement. Tuo told him the old ferry landing still appeared on one map they carried.

desert_p06_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_038.text: Du asked which edition, with an urgency that made everyone laugh. A closed kitchen was another altered landmark, smaller than a collapsed causeway but capable of sending hungry people a long way in the wrong direction. Yue asked whether the cook wanted the changed landing marked in the public corrections. He did, provided the note named his mother's present stall as well. Du promised to ask the date and location on return rather than printing hearsay from a supper bowl. The cook looked pleased that his family could enter a map without becoming a grand story.

desert_p06_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_039.text: He described the stall's blue awning, the way she fried herbs with flatbread, and the old wooden ferry bell beside her counter. Long Legs regretted hearing all this after finishing his own meal. Bao said hunger for a remembered breakfast was not an emergency. Later, while supper cooled enough to eat, Yue used the practice lead from her own pack for a brief supervised session with Gao's calibrated receiving cup. Bao checked the unbroken skin where the padded contact would sit above her ankle.

desert_p06_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_040.text: The lower paired routes were already earned; the unfamiliar part was using this field apparatus while tired from travel. Gao had her sit with the leg supported and choose a small task only. The first useful quarter unit arrived through the third pair after four measured breaths and a half-unit input. Yue released it cleanly before looking at the reading. The warmth travelled inward through the trained lower route, reached its ordinary hip junction, and returned along the complementary path without spilling into the neighbouring pair.

desert_p06_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_041.text: It felt less like a new possession than a conversation whose words she had finally learned to stop clearly. The cup's mark rested inside its expected band. Gao wrote the reading and asked Yue what changed when she removed her desire to make it impressive. Yue said her knee stopped tightening. Bao touched the supporting cushion and said that was a useful answer, more informative than declaring everything effortless.

desert_p06_042.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p06_042.text: Rest before the second. We are checking how the fourth pair behaves in this posture, not collecting a row of flattering marks. Drink your supper portion when it arrives. The reference card remains beside the cup so neither of us has to remember its limits through pride. You have trained these routes under people who watched them carefully. Keep that habit outside the examination room. I value a clean interruption as much as a good reading. When a caravan tool asks for a small pulse, it generally has a reason for preferring one.

desert_p06_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_043.text: Yue waited until the first warmth faded and her ordinary breathing returned. Then she settled the fourth pair, distinct from the third in its control. Four breaths admitted the same half unit; the cup accepted the rated quarter of useful work. She interrupted on Gao's signal, held still while the return settled, and described the difference in tension around her ankle. The two tasks together had spent one unit from her body's available charge. She wrote that cost in her own notes. The number was modest, and its modesty made the successful control feel honest.

desert_p06_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_044.text: Bao found no pain or return of the old shoulder strain. Yue's travel fatigue remained ordinary and deserved sleep rather than another test. Gao closed the receiving cup and returned the lead to its owner. She said either lower pair could supply that particular light input under the same supervised setup, provided Yue was rested and the contact remained sound. The qualification did not become a caravan rank or a licence to operate every device in the ruin. It became one more specific thing she could do.

desert_p06_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_045.text: Yue packed the lead carefully, pleased enough that she did not need to invent a larger title. Du had watched from the map table without pretending not to. He asked whether the movement could be drawn. Yue sketched the known outward and returning lower routes in her private book, leaving the finer training marks out of the public field pages. He examined the plain shape and said surveyors also spent years learning which neighbouring line not to join. Gao accused him of attempting to recruit every useful metaphor into cartography. He said it was a broad discipline.

desert_p06_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_046.text: Bao took away his cold bowl and returned it warmed, which quieted the scholarly contest more effectively than any conclusion. The camp worker sat nearby with his bound wrist resting against a rolled cloak. He asked whether training made recovery less inconvenient. Yue said it made her more aware of what needed recovery, which could feel like the opposite. He laughed and said his hammer arm had learned the same lesson in a much cheaper school. She offered to write the short message he wanted sent on their return.

desert_p06_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_047.text: He dictated that he was working, eating well, and had been told to let somebody else strike the stakes. His wife would identify the missing explanation immediately, he admitted. Yue asked whether to include the strained wrist. He thought about it, then said yes, with Bao's judgement that it was improving and the actual restrictions. The fuller line made him look less brave and more believable. He signed with his good hand. Yue folded the note and placed it in his own bag.

desert_p06_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_048.text: Its destination had nothing to do with the carrier report, but it belonged to the return journey just as firmly. Around them the evening meal resumed. Gao accepted the last boiled egg and broke it in half for Bao, who claimed the larger piece without a trace of medical hesitation. Han had seen the two calibrated pulses and asked Yue whether the field arrangement differed from her kiln practice. She described the lighter cup and the change in posture. He listened without reaching for the stage cord at her collar or asking whether she could move a tank.

desert_p06_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_049.text: His daughter had once explained a school mechanism to him, he said, and insisted he stop naming everything with a wheel a cart. He was trying to extend the lesson. Yue liked that answer. It treated the trained work as work, with details that mattered, rather than as a new form of entertainment. Before the next conversation began, Yue put her practice notes away. The new pairs remained part of her life even when the day's chief demand was a pencil held steadily beside another person's pain. She had imagined fifth stage might make ordinary work feel smaller.

desert_p06_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_050.text: Instead it gave her another scale on which small things could be done well. Her feet were still dusty. Her sandal still needed adjustment. The house still stood beyond her capacity to understand at a glance. She ate the warm broth and found none of those facts diminished the progress she had earned. After supper Gao compared the two lower-route readings with the reference-stone baseline. The cup's acceptance remained consistent, giving tomorrow's light tasks a recent calibration record. Yue had already spent one unit on practice and needed no third trial.

desert_p06_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_051.text: She watched Gao cover the card so dew would not soften its pencil marks. Du, sorting his tracings nearby, observed that the instrument was fortunate never to have wished for applause. Gao said it had other expensive preferences, including dry bedding. She returned the receiving cup to its padded compartment and recorded the remaining reference charge. Bao sent the workers to check feet and shoulders before darkness. Yue's blister was settling under the adjusted sandal strap, and her palms needed only thin protective cloth now. The camp worker's wrist would still limit hammering tomorrow.

desert_p06_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_052.text: Han kept that note on the work page, moving no labour back merely because the day had gone well. The farrier examined the six mules and found Plum tired but sound. She had pulled through the rough ridge without favouring a foot. Her driver brushed the sweat marks carefully, each stroke carrying away dust that might otherwise rub beneath tomorrow's harness. The house grew louder as the air cooled. Its notes did not form a tune exactly, but one recurring interval resembled the wooden bird's first two sounds.

desert_p06_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_053.text: The driver answered it once, then felt ridiculous and put the toy away. Tuo asked him to try again. He did, softer. The old walls replied only when the next gust reached the shaft. For a moment camp listened to the awkward conversation between a child's present and an abandoned machine. Du did not write a sentence about memory. Yue noticed his empty hand and was glad he had let the moment remain theirs. Gao and Han disagreed near the map table after the others settled.

desert_p06_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_054.text: Han wanted the lower-site approach measured and the caravan ready to depart the following afternoon. Gao wanted one extra morning to compare its drainage channels with the wind station, because those channels might explain the route's present instability. Du said nothing at first. Tuo watched them both. The supply gave room for a bounded extension, not several days of speculative digging. Gao proposed a half-day inspection with an agreed stopping point. Han asked what finding would justify staying. She answered that a usable old route control or a concealed water source would change the carrier report.

desert_p06_055.speaker: han_xun
desert_p06_055.text: I need a finding we can recognise, not a reason to remain until curiosity grows tired. Measure the lower approach tomorrow. If you find something that changes whether loaded carts can use it, we discuss the additional morning. If the chambers merely contain interesting shelves, we draw what is visible and leave them for people hired to examine shelves. I am not deaf to history. I also have twelve names on a return account. Those names belong to people whose families would prefer an ordinary disappointing report to an extraordinary unfinished journey.

desert_p06_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_056.text: Gao accepted the conditions, but her expression stayed sharp. Han's worry could sound like a judgement on her professionalism when he repeated it often enough. She told him that. He sat back, surprised, then said he had spent the day fearing the patient's wagon would take Bao and leave them responsible for choices outside their capacity. The fear had lingered after the handover. Gao's face eased without losing all its edge. She said she would make the stopping point explicit in the morning work plan. Han thanked her. An argument about time had finally named the anxiety using its voice.

desert_p06_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_057.text: When Han and Gao finished their argument about tomorrow, Du brought the subscriber sketch to the lamp again. A small mark beside its northern stair looked like a bird until he turned the paper sideways. It was a scale sign, indicating the old weigh house. The copied caption had dropped that sign's explanation. Han had received the sketch from a carrier who received it from a store clerk, neither claiming to have drawn it. The missing caption now mattered more than anybody's handwriting. Gao recorded the chain of copies before identifying the image too firmly from its surviving mark.

desert_p06_058.speaker: du_she
desert_p06_058.text: There is a way to make a map wrong without adding a false line: remove the sentence that tells people how to read the true ones. This little sign once separated a scale station from a wind station. It became decoration in the second copy and disappeared from the letter. I should have asked for the original. So should the carrier office. We can still ask when we return. For tomorrow, the physical features will guide us more safely than blaming three clerks who were each handed a sheet somebody else called sufficient.

desert_p06_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_059.text: Tuo examined the mark and said the lower exchange had a carved balance over one doorway. She remembered seeing it from the path near the split cairn. Du's sketch might indeed belong there. The knowledge did not grant them a safe interior or an intact loading floor. It did give the morning route a purpose precise enough to resist wandering. Han rewrote the first line of the commission note: locate the lower exchange and compare its approach with the supplied sketch. Gao added the exterior stopping point. Their earlier tension settled into a page whose tasks could actually end.

desert_p06_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_060.text: Yue noticed a faint smudge on the sketch's back. It preserved part of an earlier caption, transferred when damp paper had been folded. Du held it toward the lamp without placing it over the flame. Two letters suggested a northern district archive, but the rest could not be read. He copied the visible strokes and refused to restore the missing institution. A surviving source might explain the old station group later. It was another question to take home, not a reason to turn the present camp into an excavation. Han seemed relieved when Du said that first.

desert_p06_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_061.text: Outside the lamplight, the quiet driver repaired a loose buckle tongue. Yue held the shade while she worked so moths would not circle directly through her eyes. The driver said maps made people argue about what they expected, while buckles made them argue about what had happened. Both could keep a person awake. She had once driven the public ridge in a winter snow that concealed every familiar edge. Tuo guided the team by the exposed dark outcrops and turned back before the final shelf. Their customer complained. The driver still considered it one of the guide's best journeys.

desert_p06_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_062.text: Yue asked whether Tuo thought so too. The woman smiled and said Tuo had spent three days calling it a tedious retreat. People rarely praised their own sensible disappointment. She slid the new buckle pin into place, tested it twice, and handed Yue the lamp. The mules shifted nearby, making small comfortable sounds through their noses. A caravan returned by ordinary roads could look unremarkable to the people who paid for adventure. Yue wondered how many unremarkable returns had required difficult courage. Her new stage record named what she had achieved. Nothing comparable hung from Tuo's collar.

desert_p06_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_063.text: Tuo came over while Yue was still thinking and asked for the lamp. She wanted one last look at the marked hollow slab before everyone slept. The driver joined them, carrying no tool that might tempt an unnecessary repair. The boundary cord remained visible from the tents. Gao's two small stakes cast shadows across the pale paving. A moth settled on the nearest one. Tuo moved an empty bowl left beside the line, then looked at Yue's face and asked what solemn thought had found her. Yue answered honestly about the winter retreat.

desert_p06_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_064.text: Tuo made a noise halfway between laughter and impatience.

desert_p06_065.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p06_065.text: A good retreat is dull by the time you get home. That is its best quality. People alive and annoyed can tell me I was overcautious; I am willing to give them the opportunity. Do not build me a monument out of one old driver's story. I have hurried when I should have waited, and remembered wrong at inconvenient moments. You saw me look at the cloth today as though it could reverse years. We improve the road by noticing each other, not by choosing one person to become a perfect guide in everybody's head.

desert_p06_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_066.text: Yue accepted the rebuke because its roughness protected the conversation from praise too large to carry. Tuo handed the lamp back and pointed toward the north stair. The deeper rushing sound had begun beneath the higher notes, audible now even without a gust across camp. The guide thought another outlet faced the basin. Gao would compare directions tomorrow. They stood listening for a while, saying little. The sound was ordinary air arranged by old stone. It still made the house feel larger than its broken walls.

desert_p06_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_067.text: Yue put that impression in her private notes without promoting it into a measured fact. Han extinguished the table lamp after storing the public copies in a dry case. Du kept the older papers beneath his own headrest, a habit he admitted was terrible for their corners. Gao told him to use the padded box. He said he would, then actually did when she waited. Yue watched the little compliance with amusement. Scholars could defend a habit for forty years and abandon it when a former pupil remained standing in the right place.

desert_p06_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_068.text: The night wind shifted, lowering the house's note. Bao closed her treatment case and went to check the camp worker's wrist once more. Tuo suggested they all sleep before writing a treaty with the sunset. Du agreed too quickly, which made Gao turn on him with a laugh. He confessed he had been waiting for somebody else to propose bed while he pretended a scholar's immunity to fatigue. Yue packed the tracings into their separate envelope and put the plain field book beside her blanket. The wind station's northern window was dark now. Its bird had vanished inside the nest.

desert_p06_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_069.text: Beyond the courtyard, the split cairn lay invisible against the ridge, holding tomorrow's road between two names that would need more than memory to separate. The camp settled in pieces. A driver coughed dust from his throat, drank a small amount from his portion, and lay down. The cook counted the breakfast eggs before remembering there were none left to count. He looked affronted by his own preparedness and packed the pot instead. Yue brushed grit from her cloak, leaving the folds loose enough to dry. The grass sample had become brittle at its cut end.

desert_p06_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_070.text: She moved it into a paper sleeve so tomorrow's walking would not grind it to powder. It was a small gift, and she wanted it to survive with its story intact. Before sleeping, Yue reread the private line about the red cloth. She had written that rescue made grief useful, and now struck the sentence out. Tuo's grief did not owe anyone usefulness. The cloth had been useful because two guides tied it where people could see; the guide had recognised it because memory hurt in unpredictable ways. Those facts were enough.

desert_p06_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_071.text: She wrote them plainly beneath the crossed line and shut the book. Outside, the wind station continued its ancient work without caring how well she described it. She was grateful, for a moment, to sleep near something that asked for no applause. During the night Yue woke to a low rushing sound beneath the familiar singing. She listened until she could distinguish wind along the tent from air moving through the house's lower grille. The deeper sound continued between gusts. It might be another opening facing a different direction, or something moving below the stones.

desert_p06_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_072.text: She did not go alone to investigate. In the morning she told Gao exactly when she had heard it and how it differed. The surveyor wrote the observation for the lower-site comparison. A night sound could begin a question without requiring someone to answer it in darkness. At first light the crew ate while the courtyard remained cool. Han repeated the agreed exterior work and possible bounded extension once, then stopped. Gao assigned Yue the light rod, Du the older location sheets, and Tuo the approach. Bao would remain at camp with the drivers and check the rest arrangements.

desert_p06_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p06_073.text: The four walked toward the split cairn along a path used by people rather than loaded carts. The dark ridge hid the sun. When they reached the cairn's first half, Yue saw that its second half stood farther east than the map's single black dot had suggested.
